lines.text: One call to a heating installer, played twice.
Ten fifteen. Lies calls. No heating, two small kids.
The line is busy. She'll get a callback.
After lunch, Nadia calls back, and moves another customer.
Then she phones that customer, Lies again, and Jens.
On site, Jens finds the real fault: the compressor.
That evening, he mails his notes to Sara.
On Thursday, Sara retypes them into a quote, and lowers the labour.
On Friday, Wim approves it, from his desk.
The quote reaches Lies the next week.
Four decisions. Fourteen hand-offs by people.
Same call. Now on Aeolus.
Ten fifteen. The line is busy, so the voice agent answers.
The planning agent finds two o'clock, if another visit moves.
Nadia decides. Both customers are told.
Jens's phone has the brief, and the sensor is in his van.
On site, he finds the compressor.
His voice note becomes a report, a parts order and a quote.
Sara lowers the labour for a ten-year customer.
Wim approves it from the side of a football pitch.
Lies accepts. Repair booked, parts ordered, invoice sent.
All done before five.
Same call. Same four decisions, by people.
Fourteen hand-offs by people, or none.
Human intelligence where it counts. Full speed everywhere else.
Aeolus. The open network for people, apps and agents.
